message:
test(build): check that the shipped helper has no test switch to strip

Test 1, build 1. No product change. This is the gate the reviewer asked for, in the only form
that fits what was actually built.

The deadline work needed a capture that never answers. The expected shape was a hidden argument on
GNLinkCapture plus a build gate to keep it out of the shipping binary. What it does instead is
stage a scratch directory and put a different executable there under that name -- the host resolves
its helper beside itself, so the production code picks up whatever is there. Nothing was added to
the product, so there is nothing to strip.

That is a claim about a binary, and it should not rest on anyone remembering. This reads the built
GNLinkCapture.exe and looks for nine shapes such a switch would take, as bytes and as UTF-16.

The part that makes the silence mean anything: it also has to FIND things. Five real switches --
--thumbnail, --mapping, --done-event, --frame-event, --hwnd -- are asserted present, because a
scanner that found nothing because it was broken would otherwise report a clean bill. If those
stop passing, the absences are declared worthless in the same run.

And the gate catches what it is for: adding --test-stall-ms to the helper's argument parser makes
three of the checks fail. Reverted, 16 of 16 again.
